content:
sophie: FYI raised by customer via email — user says they suddenly get 403 when accessing project console after their IdP team applied an update. they can still authenticate to other apps.
sophie: customer reports: 'I click into our Redwood project and see \"You do not have permission to view this project (403)\". Our SSO shows group membership intact.'
marcus: ok copying the ticket here. first guess SCIM mapping or group GUID change. did they change the group name or migrate to a new IdP instance?
april: I asked for the IdP audit — they said they merged two groups in Okta and removed a legacy group. SCIM sync ran ~1h before the customer reported issue.
sophie: I tried repro with a test user — after SCIM group-merge the user's console shows 403 even though API /v1/projects lists the project and the user's email is in the membership list returned by our internal API. weird.
marcus: can you paste the raw SCIM event payloads? specifically looking for group.id vs members[].value changes.
sophie: pasted logs: ```
INFO 2026-03-14 14:02:31 scim: PATCH /Groups/9f2a -> { Operations: [{ "op": "replace", "path": "members", "value": [{"value":"4f3c"}, {"value":"f6a9"}] } ] }
INFO 2026-03-14 14:02:32 scim: Group 9f2a renamed to "prod-team (merged)"
INFO 2026-03-14 14:02:33 scim: Member 4f3c removed, member f6a9 added
```
april: aha — our linking in Redis uses the original SCIM group id (9f2a) to map to a Redwood role id. when the group was merged we did a PATCH that removed the original member entries and the group id remained the same but internal member.value ids changed. however I also see a separate event a few minutes later: ```
INFO 2026-03-14 14:03:40 scim: DELETE /Groups/9f2a -> 204 No Content
INFO 2026-03-14 14:03:41 scim: POST /Groups -> { id: "c0ffee" name: "prod-team" }
```
april: so the group got deleted and recreated with a new SCIM id (c0ffee). our sync job didn't clear the old mapping and our permission check path still looks at the mapping for 9f2a -> role:project_write. user now belongs to c0ffee which has no mapping -> 403.
marcus: makes sense. that explains 'members list contains email but permission check uses group id mapping'. short term workaround: reassign role to the recreated group in console or run the re-sync script to rebuild mappings.
sophie: customer asked for immediate fix. I ran a re-sync for their org: `./bin/scim-sync --org 12345 --force` and logs show it picked up group c0ffee and created mapping to the same role (role_id: r-789). they report restore of access.
oncall-bot: Incident bot: restart of scim-worker in prod initiated by sophie at 2026-03-14T15:05:02Z
marcus: long term we should detect group-delete+recreate patterns and reconcile by group name/email before creating orphan mapping. filing RO ticket to eng-runtime.
april: also propose adding a heuristic: if group.name matches an existing mapping within 24h of a DELETE+POST, treat as rename and preserve mapping (or create alias). I'll add a design note.
sophie: customer is happy, closing their ticket after verifying access. asked to notify us if they see more.
marcus: follow-up tasks: 1) add a monitoring alert for sudden spike in orphan group creations; 2) add retention to SCIM mapping table to keep tombstones for 48h; 3) design + PR for aliasing.
april: I'll open the alert + sprint ticket.
sophie: thanks team :raised_hands: leaving recording of steps in the support case: 1) ask IdP for audit of group operations; 2) run scim-sync --force for org; 3) if immediate access required reassign role manually via console; 4) escalate to eng if repeated.
marcus: good writeup. adding to knowledge base under 'SCIM group recreated -> 403 access' (internal doc).
sophie: closing thread.
